run.procedureSummary:
Start: water 3,6,6,2,2,1; all pumps LAMINAR; tally 0. Each cycle runs five steps, and each step is finished on all six compartments before the next step starts.
Step 1, take on water: add the full table amount to each compartment, even if that takes it over volume.
Step 2, scuppers: go through compartments 1 to 6 one at a time. Anything over volume moves into the next compartment (k+1) before that one is checked, so overflow can cascade. Overflow from 6 goes overboard to the tally.
Step 3, pump check, on the water left after the scuppers: a LAMINAR pump with water >= its inception mark becomes CAVITATING. A CAVITATING pump with water <= its desinence mark becomes LAMINAR. Otherwise nothing changes. Each change is logged.
Step 4, pump: first work out every amount from the current contents, using the states just set in step 3. A LAMINAR pump sends floor(w/4) overboard. A CAVITATING pump sends floor(w/2) forward into compartment k-1; compartment 1's backflow goes overboard. Then all six moves are applied together, with no volume cap.
Step 5, emergency blow: total all six. Only if the total is strictly above 38, each compartment keeps floor(w/2) and the rest goes overboard; the cycle is noted.
Report: end quantities and states after step 5 of cycle 5. Balance check: starting water + water taken on = end water + tally.

openPoints.point: Which state the pump step uses in the cycle where a state changes
openPoints.assumption: The step-3 state from the same cycle governs step 4, because step 3 comes first.
'Forward toward the bow' means compartment k sends water to k-1, and compartment 1 sends it overboard to the tally.

openPoints.point: Pump amounts versus water arriving by backflow in the same step
openPoints.assumption: All six amounts are worked out from the contents before any move (taken literally from the write-up). Water that arrives by backflow is not pumped again until the next cycle.

openPoints.point: What the blow rule totals, and the case of exactly 38
openPoints.assumption: The blow totals the contents after the pump step. The rule fires only if the total is above 38. In cycle 5 the total was exactly 38, so the blow did not fire.
Each compartment keeps floor(w/2) and the remainder, ceil(w/2), goes overboard to the tally.
The end quantities are reported as they stand after cycle 5 with no final scupper pass. Compartment 2 ends at 10, above its volume of 8, as the write-up allows.

openPoints.point: Where scupper overflow from compartment 6 goes
openPoints.assumption: It goes overboard and is counted on the tally (the write-up says 'Everything overboard goes on the tally').
